title: La Carmélite
summary: La Carmélite by Ernest Daudet is a novel written in the late 19th century. The opening of the novel paints the convent’s stark serenity before tracing Nicolette’s fervent decision to enter the Carmel, affirmed by the prioress and sealed in prayer. At home, the contrast with her sister Irène’s gilded yet loveless marriage sharpens, until a midnight crisis explodes: Malivert surprises Irène with Frédéric, shots are fired, and Irène drags the officer into Nicolette’s room, begging her to claim him. To save her sister, Nicolette declares the man her suitor and bears the scandal. Shaken, she seeks counsel from Abbé Cardenne, who urges her to complete the sacrifice by marrying. Frédéric’s family formally proposes; in guarded garden conversations, Nicolette sets strict terms—respect for her vow until the Church releases it, freedom for rigorous piety, and his moral amendment—while Irène masks her remorse.
